The present Writ Petition has been filed for the issuance of a Writ of Certiorarified Mandamus to quash the impugned order dated 09.10.2024 passed in Na.Ka.A1/976/2024 by the 9th respondent by fixing the compensation as Rs. 4,00,000/- and direct the respondents to disburse fair compensation of Rs. 25,00,000/- on account of the demise of the petitioners minor son Mohammed Usman (Male /13 years).

2.1 The brief facts as stated in the affidavit are that the petitioner is 8th standard pass-out and a small trader doing some local sales in Bengaluru, but suffering from spinal cord disc bulge issues on his back side for a long time.

The petitioner is married to one Rizwana Parveen, aged 40 years and has 2 sons namely Muhammad Usman aged 12 and Muhammad Affaan aged 1 and they are residing in Pallapatti Municipality which has 30,000 population as per 2011 census.
The petitioner's son first son was born on 12.10.2012 and he is a bright and outstanding student of class 7th standard of Pallapatti Higher Secondary https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
( Uploaded on: 13/08/2025 12:11:58 pm ) School.
On 08.10.2024 while he was returning from his school, he got drowned and died in the open sewage drainage by around 4.30 p.m.
On the day of the incident, it was heavily raining since 3.45 p.m. started reducing by around 4.30 p.m. but the drizzling continued for almost 7-8 hours on the same day.
Hence the roads, streets, lanes and drainages were inundated with rain water.
The school has allowed the students to go home around 4.30 p.m.
Without any intimation to the petitioner, the petitioner son had started returning from the school by bicycle while it was still drizzling.

At the same time, the school administrations of various other schools in Pallapatti have informed the parents over phone about the whereabouts of their wards while no such information was given to them from Pallapatti Higher Secondary School.
Hence the petitioner was under the impression that they son was safe inside the school campus.

2.2. While that being so, the petitioner had received a call around 4.30 p.m. from one of resident in the same street that their son had fallen into the open sewage drainage just opposite to ICICI Bank in Pallapatti alongside Thadicombu- Pallapatti - Aravaurichi (SH 193) State Highways.
The land on which drainage is situated belongs to State Highways Department, but maintenance works are done by Pallapatti Municipality.
The petitioner immediately rushed to the spot wherein the bicycle and school bag was found but https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
the petitioner's son was missing.

It was informed by the people gathered that their son had fallen into the open drainage after getting stuck into the broken cement roads inside their street lane in E.A. Mansoor Ali vs The Additional Chief Secretary ... on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29984811/
3 Habeeb Nagar connecting their home with State Highways.

sentences.text: The petitioner immediately contacted the Fire station, Police and Municipal Administration for rescue and they started searching.
Around 6.30 p.m. they could locate the body in Nanganchi river almost 750 meters away from the spot.
Then body was taken to the nearest Pallapatti Government Hospital where he was declared dead by the doctors.
2.3. The respondents registered FIR in Crime No.387 dated 08.10.2024 on the file of Aravakurichi Police Station.
The post mortem was done on 09.10.2024 and the body was handed over to the petitioner on 09.10.2024.
The District Collector, Karur visited the home on 10.10.2024 and paid exgratia compensation of Rs. 4,00,000 (Rupees Four lakhs only) under State Disaster Relief Fund.

2.4 The contention of the petitioner is that the Local Authority and Highways failed to maintain the Open Sewage Drainage and the School Authorities who had let the students out at the time of heavy rain are responsible for the negligent act.

Further contention of the petitioner is that even under Motor Accidents Claim the petitioner is entitled to Rs.12,60,000/- as compensation,
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 13/08/2025 12:11:58 pm ) besides other compensation for (1) Love and Affection, (2) Funeral Expenses, (3) Transport Charges, (4) Loss of Line of Descendants, (5) Future Prosperity, (6) Psychological Trauma.
But the respondents had paid Rs, 4,00,000/- which is degrading the human values.
The present issue cannot only be construed as a child falling in an Open/Damaged Drainage due to heavy rain, but it is purely due to the negligence on the part of the respondents.
Hence, the present writ petition is filed for further compensation.
3.1. The 7th respondent has filed a counter affidavit wherein it is stated that the compensation for a sum of Rs. 25,00,000/- (Twenty Five Lakhs Rupees) is baseless.

Since the minor who lost his life only because of the sudden heavy rainfall on the date of occurrence, wherein the boy fell into the drainage and due to continuous rain, the minor was not able to withstand, hence carried away into the Nangangi river.
The said incident happened only because of natural calamity and not because of the negligence of the respondents.

Since the said incident was treated by the Tahsildar, Aravakurichi as Natural Disaster, immediate measures and steps were taken and recommended for compensation based on G.O.Ms.No. 579 Revenue & D.M (DM.III(2)) Dept. dated 09.10.2023 and as per G.O.Ms.No.12 Revenue & Disaster Management Wing DM II Section dated 12.01.2024.

The date of occurrence is 08.10.2024 and the compensation of Rs. https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 13/08/2025 12:11:58 pm ) 4,00,000/- was immediately credited on 10.10.2024 in the Account No. 6032429451 of Indian Bank, Pallapatti, Account Holder, Mrs. Rizwana Parveen wife of Mansoor Ali.

The G.O.Ms.No.579 Revenue & D.M (DM.III(2)) Dept. dated 09.12.2023 had enacted and came into force by revising the earlier norms and to envisage granting enhanced relief to the victims of Natural Calamities under State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) and the National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF) in the form of financial assistance for loss of lives, loss of limb, eyes, grievous injuries,
loss of crops, cattle, damages to house on Natural Calamities.
Further it was clearly mentioned in the said G.O. that a sum of Rs. 4,00,000/- was fixed as exgratia payment to families of deceased persons on Natural calamities.
As per Section 12 of the DM Act empowers the NDMA to recommend guidelines for minimum standards of relief to persons affected by a disaster.
In terms thereof, the NDMA issued guidelines for minimum standards of relief.
As per these guidelines, norms were E.A. Mansoor Ali vs The Additional Chief Secretary ...

The following minimum standard of relief, inter alia, are applicable as per the Home Ministry's letter No. 327/2024 dated 08.04.2015.

(i) Ex-gratia payment to families of deceased persons to the extent of Rs. 4,00,000/- Hence the relief which was asked by the petitioner to fix a fair compensation based on Motor Accident claim formula or under any other formula https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 13/08/2025 12:11:58 pm )
cannot be legally granted since the said incident is a Natural calamity and hence the Respondents are not in a position to disburse or to make account to refix the compensation against the existing Government Order.
3.2.
The petitioner himself had admitted that on the date of occurrence there was heavy rain and drizzling.
And also admitted a sum of Rs. 4,00,000/- credited as compensation to the deceased family.
Hence the allegation that the incident occurred due to negligence of the respondents is incorrect and false.
The prayer for suitable job under compassionate ground cannot be granted since there is no provision for granting any job.
Also, there is no provision to bear educational expenses to the second son.
Further fixing compensation under Motor Vehicle Claim for a sum of Rs.25,00,000/- is not applicable.
Hence, the 7th respondent prayed to dismiss the writ petition.

4. The 8th respondent has filed counter affidavit wherein it is stated that the road is known as Dindigul Road in Pallapatti Town, which belongs to State Highways Department as custodian of the road, passing through the Pallapatti Town.
The road including the drainage channel on the sides is vested with the State Highways Department in the aspect of ownership, maintenance and repairs.
The said authority has passed the impugned order which is under challenge before this Court.

The Pallapatti Municipality has no role in https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 13/08/2025 12:11:58 pm ) maintaining the said road except for the purpose of conservancy namely street sweeping over the same.
All other aspects of the said road are carried out by the 10th respondent and his subordinates.
This respondent hereby adopts the Counter affidavit that is filed by the Respondents 1 to 7, 9 and 10 in so far as the same is not contrary to the interests and jurisdiction of this Respondent.
Further it is stated that the channel is storm water drain channel meant to carry the flow of rain water to the natural water courses from the road and surrounding areas and not drainage channel.
The 10th respondent has passed the impugned order fixing the compensation as per the applicable Government Orders and the same are proper.

After the incident the 8th respondent had directed the 10th respondent to take steps to cover the channels along the highway road within the Municipal limits as the same is a danger to the safety of the residents.
5. The 10th Respondent has filed a counter affidavit wherein it is stated that the petitioner had filed the present petition for higher compensation.
Admittedly, the petitioner's son had ridden his bicycle while raining.
Unfortunately fallen into the open drainage.
The petitioner had raised various allegations about the entire system, but it is an unfortunate accident occurred due to the natural calamity.

The accident happened due to non-maintenance of sewage is utter false, since even in the averments in the FIR would show that it was an https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on:
13/08/2025 12:11:58 pm ) accident due to heavy rainfall, which is an Act of God.
If an adult was in the said situation, then the person would be careful, since the deceased was kid unknowingly fell into the channel.
The loss to the petitioner is undisputedly high, however, the same cannot be E.A. Mansoor Ali vs The Additional Chief Secretary ...

5 equated with availing monetary benefits by the way of compensation from State Exchequer.

The subject open drain is being maintained by the 8th respondent municipality and it is for the municipality to maintain the sewage drains and the respondent highways department have no say in respect to the same.

Hence, the liability ought to be fastened against the municipal authorities if at all any negligence had been proven, since, the role of the respondent department is merely to construction and maintenance of the road alone and nothing else.
There is no question of maintenance of drainages by the highways department that too the drainage falls under the purview of municipality.
Hence, it is clear that the allegations by the petitioner are omnibus in nature.

Admittedly, there was a heavy rainfall in the said area for about 2 to 3 hours, obviously the entire area would have been flooded and the similar is the scenario even in the developed countries on receipt of such a heavy rainfall.
Moreover, the petitioner's son had fallen in the sewage due to his carelessness alone, since, no such incident had been reported in the subject area till date.

If at all the petitioner's son had fallen due to the potholes in the road, then the respondent department ought to have been fastened with the liability, however, no https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on:
13/08/2025 12:11:58 pm ) such allegations had been raised by the petitioner.
Hence, it is clear that the deceased person had not been careful enough at the time of riding his cycle, which is purely an outcome of deceased person's negligence.
Contributory negligence doesn't only play a significant role in absolving the respondent of his liability but also the assessment of damages.
For a tort of negligence to be contributory in nature, it ought to be in the proximate cause of actual injury to qualify as contributory negligence.

If the prima facie facts and evidence relating to the case show the petitioner's deceased son has contributed to injury by doing negligent act on his part (Novus actus interveniens), then he can't bring an action for recovery of damages.

Further for a tort to be constituted as contributory negligence there are certain requirements which are needed to be met,
For a certain tort to be constituted as contributory negligence there are certain requirements which are needed to be met.

There are three broader rules which are meant to be proven by the respondent are:
a.
Firstly, it must be shown that that the petitioner's son was exposed to some unreasonable risk against which a reasonable person would take precautions.
There is no such question has arisen, since, there was no pending work on the part of the respondent department.

b. Then it must be shown that the safety device in question is generally effective either in reducing the risk of an accident, or alternatively in reducing the damage that would normally https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 13/08/2025 12:11:58 pm ) result if that risk materialized.
c. Thirdly, it must be shown that the device was available to the deceased, but since the petitioner's son was riding a bicycle at the time of heavy rainfall, no such question arisen.
When the above are absent in the present case, hence the petitioner is not entitled any enhancement of compensation.
Hence the 10th respondent prayed to dismiss the writ petition.

Heard Mr.K.R.Laxman, the Learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner, Mr.S.Selvaganesan, the Learned Additional Government Pleader appearing for the respondents 1 to 7 & 9 to 11, Mr.J.Parekh Kumar, the Learned Standing Counsel appearing for the 8th respondent and Mr.Y.T.Asraf, the Learned Counsel appearing for the 12th respondent and perused the records.
7.
After hearing the rival submissions, this Court had given its anxious consideration.
The primary contention of the petitioner is that the respondents have not maintained the storm water drain properly, especially the respondents have not closed the drain.
For which the petitioner had relied on the photos.

It is seen after the incident, the open rain water storm drain was closed with cement s l a b s b u t w i t h g a p s . F u r t h e r i t i s s e e n t h e a c c i d e n t o c c u r r e d w h e n t h e
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
( Uploaded on: 13/08/2025 12:11:58 pm ) deceased child struck in the damaged road, then fell in the drain, but the deceased bicycle and school bag are very much available near the incident.
If rain was not there then the deceased child would not have been washed away.
He might have sustained some injuries.
When there is open rain water drain, then any person ought to have been careful.
Since it is 10 years old child, the deceased child could not manage the situation after he was struck in the damaged road.
The above observation on events would indicate that the road was not maintained properly and the rain water storm was not closed with slabs.
Therefore, both the Highways and the Local Authority are at negligence and the contention of the respondents that the respondents are no way responsible is rejected.
Hence the petitioner is entitled to increase in the compensation.
8. However, the deceased child ought not to have travelled while the vigor of the rain was not subsided, hence the parents are responsible for contributory negligence.

Further, as held supra if the rain was not there then the deceased child would have sustained injuries, but would not have washed away, hence the natural forces working at that the time are also contributing to the death of the child.
Hence the increase of the compensation ought to be fixed after taking into account these factors.
9 . N o w t h e i s s u e o f f i x i n g o f c o m p e n s a t i o n o u g h t t o b e c o n s i d e r e d .
I t https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
( Uploaded on: 13/08/2025 12:11:58 pm ) is seen that the petitioner had already received a sum of Rs.4,00,000/- from the Chief Minister's contingency fund.
This indicates that the respondents have taken note of the situation seriously and had paid the compensation.
Further the respondents have laid proper road and now the open drain is fully closed with cement.
This would again indicate that the respondents have acted responsibly.
On one hand the loss of the petitioner cannot be measured in terms of money.

On the other hand, the compensation granted in meagre.
10.
Therefore, this Court is fixing the compensation to Rs.8,00,000/-.
Since the respondents had paid Rs.4,00,000/-, the balance payable is Rs. 4,00,000/- The said amount shall be paid within a period of 12 weeks from the date of receipt of the copy of the order.
If not paid within the stipulated time, from the date of default the amount shall carry interest of 6% per annum.
11. With the above observations, this Writ Petition is allowed.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Consequently, the connected miscellaneous petition is closed.

Firstly, it must be shown that that the petitioner's son was exposed to some unreasonable risk against which a reasonable person would take precautions.
There is no such question has arisen, since, there was no pending work on the part of the respondent department.
b. Then it must be shown that the safety device in question is generally effective either in reducing the risk of an accident, or alternatively in reducing the damage that would normally https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 13/08/2025 12:11:58 pm ) result if that risk materialized.
c. Thirdly, it must be shown that the device was available to the deceased, but since the petitioner's son was riding a bicycle at the time of heavy rainfall, no such question arisen.
Hence the petitioner is entitled to increase in the compensation.
Hence the increase of the compensation ought to be fixed after taking into account these factors.
